newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 4.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
SUNDAY VIMA

-- Analysis of the effects of the rise of the dollar/drachma rate reveals that apart from a slight increase in producer cost and retail price inflation, there will be gains for large segments of the Greek economy, including the export sector, tourism and overall international competitiveness of Greek goods and services.

-- The 1998 Budget to be presented later in the year will be drafted along the lines of the Convergence Programme. Expenses of all ministries will not be allowed to grow over the targeted 3.5 percent inflation rate. Expenses on public sector pay and pensions which account for a third of the ordinary budget will be set following negotiations with ADEDY, the trades union of public sector staff.
SUNDAY KATHIMERINI
-- Greece will focus in the years to 2000 on the provision of incentives for new jobs and labour training to raise the flexibility of its labour market.

-- The government is soon expected to announce a substantial rise in compensation to small businesses and professionals who will face eviction following the full liberalisation at the end of August 1997 of business leases.
IMERISIA
Aug 4

-- The government and the Bank of Greece are on guard for consumer price inflation which is expected to exhibit marginal improvement down to 5.0 percent in September from an estimated 5.4 percent in July and climb back to 5.4 percent in October.
Aug 2

-- The need to meet the Maastricht criteria will force Greece's finance ministry to step up its efforts to list public utilities and corporations on the Athens stock exchange and adjust their dividend pay-out to their true financial stance.
ISOTIMIA
-- OTE telecoms board of directors has scraped its policy for direct award to Greek producers of contracts for telecoms equipment supplies.
KATHIMERINI

-- The European Commission and the European Investment Bank are concerned over delays in the preparation of a master plan for the transfer of Olympic Airways' operations and ground facilities to the new Athens airport constructed at Spata, in time for the airport's February 2001 opening.
EXPRESS

-- The government has decided to impose a greater degree of transparency in the award of contracts for state supplies and works. To this extent it postponed a supply of digital lines for OTE telecom and will call in an external auditor to rule on the selection of the lowest bidder for a power plant.
KERDOS
-- The National Statistics Service will introduce a new index to monitor prices of food and other goods for household use sold through super markets.

-- Legislation on hirings in the public sector, dubbed the Peponis Law, will be expanded to public sector banks and local governments according to a draft bill submited to parliament. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
